sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Go's ability to produce a single, statically-linked binary makes it unusually well-suited for minimal Docker images. An interviewer asking about Docker for Go is really asking: do you understand how the Go toolchain's CGO flag and GOARCH/GOOS environment variables interact with container builds? Can you produce a secure, minimal image that starts in under a second and has no unnecessary attack surface?

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body: Think of a Go Docker build in two stages: (1) Build stage: use golang:1.22-alpine or golang:1.22-bookworm, set CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOOS=linux, run go build to produce a static binary. (2) Runtime stage: copy only the binary into gcr.io/distroless/static or scratch. The build stage can be large; only the tiny runtime layer is shipped. CGO_ENABLED=0 is the key flag—it forces pure Go, enabling scratch/distroless images without glibc.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body: 1. Dockerfile for Go: COPY go.mod go.sum first (Docker layer cache), then go mod download, then COPY . and go build. 2. Multi-stage builds: FROM golang AS builder, FROM scratch/distroless AS runtime, COPY --from=builder /app/server /server. 3. Distroless vs. scratch: scratch has nothing (no shell, no certs, no passwd); distroless/static adds CA certs and /etc/passwd—safer for most production services. 4. docker-compose for Go: service, build context, environment variables, depends_on with condition: service_healthy. 5. CGO and C libraries: if CGO is needed (sqlite, some crypto), use distroless/base or alpine with musl; set CGO_ENABLED=1 and use alpine build stage. 6. Non-root container: USER nobody:nobody or create a dedicated user in the Dockerfile; Kubernetes PodSecurityPolicy/PSS runAsNonRoot.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body: • 'How do you minimise the size of a Go Docker image?' → multi-stage build + CGO_ENABLED=0 + scratch or distroless/static. • 'What is CGO_ENABLED=0 and why does it matter for Docker?' → disables C binding, produces static binary with no glibc dependency, works in scratch images. • 'What is the difference between scratch and distroless?' → scratch is completely empty; distroless/static adds minimal runtime files (CA certs, /etc/passwd) for production safety. • 'How do you run a Go container as non-root in Kubernetes?' → USER directive in Dockerfile, securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true in pod spec.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: "My standard Go Dockerfile is a two-stage build. In the builder stage I use the official golang image, copy go.mod and go.sum first so Docker caches the module download layer, then copy source and build with CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux to get a static binary. The runtime stage is gcr.io/distroless/static—it gives me CA certificates and a minimal passwd file without a shell, which satisfies most security scanners. The final image is typically 10–15 MB. I add a USER nobody:nobody in the runtime stage and set COPY --chown=nobody:nobody so the process runs non-root. If the service needs CGO—for example, if it links against a C crypto library—I switch the runtime to distroless/base which includes glibc."
